title: Host reading
caption: Themes the host found most meaningful after holding the room — presence, signal vs noise, threshold, and the path from dialogue toward action.

nodes.label: Signal vs noise
nodes.essay: The anchoring question of the weekend: how do we separate distraction from what deserves attention — in news, in rooms, and in our own speech?

nodes.label: Entering not-knowing
nodes.essay: Aporia — slowing into the unknown together — versus monologues and solutions-mode that keep everyone inside ideas they already carried in.

nodes.label: The threshold
nodes.essay: Pebble as seed, silence before speech, humid air upstairs — designing an entrance that asks for intention and listening.

nodes.label: Contact
nodes.essay: Dialogue as contact improv: speaking into the shared middle with intention, feeling one another, not only reporting individual experience.

nodes.label: Presence in time
nodes.essay: How often did we speak into past, present, or future? Creating futures may need competence in the present — and imagination grounded in how the world works.

nodes.label: Dialogue to action
nodes.essay: Resonance in a room does not carry itself into action. Presence is one link; deciding, committing, and following up need structure the garden only began to offer.

nodes.label: Agreement as small talk
nodes.essay: Shared critique of capitalism and scarcity can feel deep and still stay inside familiar steps — trust-building warm-up, or stuck confirmation?

nodes.label: Dialogue as art
nodes.essay: Intention woven into speech — like a fashion collection that carries purpose — without demanding that every tentative voice arrive polished.

nodes.label: Body as instrument
nodes.essay: Listening for bodily signals among the noise — one input alongside words, status, fatigue, and habit.
